tagline.text: A mysterious island where legends, waterfalls, and sunsets linger

location.label: Location
location.text: Siquijor Province (San Juan, Lazi, Siquijor, Larena)

children.text: A small island floating off Dumaguete on Negros Island, known as the "island of mystery" for its legends of witches and herbal healers. A single motorbike lets you tour its stepped waterfalls, white sand beaches, and old churches in a single day.
Siquijor is about
1 hour
by boat from Dumaguete, southeast of Negros Island, and is one of the smallest provinces in the Philippines. At only about
70km
around, its coastal ring road can be circled in a single day by motorbike, and the island is divided among six municipalities: San Juan, Lazi, Siquijor, Larena, Maria, and Enrique Villanueva.

The island has long been known among Filipinos as the "island of witches" or the "island of mystery." Stories that Spanish sailors, seeing fireflies gathering in the island's forests at night, called it the "island of fire," along with rumors of herbal healers (mambabarang) and sorcerers living in mountain villages, helped create this image. Traditional herbal healers using herbs and prayer still practice on the island today, and a traditional herbal-medicine-making ceremony is held during Holy Week, but the Siquijor travelers actually experience tends to feel unassuming and friendly rather than frightening.

The island's signature attraction is Cambugahay Falls in Lazi. Water flowing over limestone terrain forms several tiered pools as it falls, with a jade-colored tint that photographs beautifully, and swinging out on a rope tied to a tree to drop into the water is a popular activity. Lazi is also home to the Church of San Isidro Labrador, completed around the
, and what's considered the largest surviving old convent building in the Philippines, both protected as national cultural heritage.
The western San Juan coast has a cluster of resorts, cafes, and dive shops, and watching the sunset at Paliton Beach at dusk is a highlight of any Siquijor trip. Since
late 2025

, direct small-aircraft flights from Cebu have improved accessibility, but development remains slow overall, which makes the island especially well suited to free-spirited travelers and couples who want to ride a motorbike around at a leisurely pace, enjoying beaches and waterfalls.

blocks.title: Swimming and rope-swinging at Cambugahay Falls

children.text: A tiered forest waterfall in Lazi; walking down about 130-odd steps from the parking area reveals one jade-colored pool after another. The rope swing into the water and a bamboo raft experience are available for a small fee.

Paliton Beach, a small stretch of white sand in San Juan, is the island's finest sunset spot, with the sun setting into the sea between palm trees. The coral area off the beach is also good for snorkeling.

The Church of San Isidro Labrador, built of coral stone and timber, and the huge old convent (convento) across the street, are masterpieces of Spanish colonial architecture. The convent's long timber-floored corridor is imposing by scale alone.

blocks.title: The century-old balete tree and fish spa

children.text: The giant balete (banyan) tree at Campalanas in San Juan is said to be several hundred years old; dipping your feet in the spring-fed pool beneath its roots lets tiny fish nibble at your dead skin.

At Salagdoong Beach in Maria on the island's east side, a concrete diving platform extends toward the sea, letting you jump from a few meters up. The surrounding forest and beach park are spacious, making it popular as a picnic spot too.
Cantabon Cave in the island's central highlands is an exploration route where you walk through a water-filled cave with a guide, relying on headlamps, amid stalactites and stalagmites. It takes
1–2 hours
, and you should expect to get your clothes wet.
The coral walls off San Juan and Siquijor town have plenty of turtles and small reef fish, making them good entry points for diving, and dive shops also run expedition dives to nearby Apo Island.

blocks.title: A glimpse of herbal healing culture

children.text: Between Good Friday and Holy Saturday during Holy Week, healers in the San Antonio village area hold a ceremony gathering herbs to make traditional medicine. At other times of year, souvenir shops sell herbal oils (love potions) that are fun to buy as a novelty.

Head to Dumaguete from Siquijor Port or Larena Port (pay the tourism eco-fee on departure)
The most common route is a flight of about
1 hour 20 minutes
from Manila to Dumaguete–Sibulan Airport (DGT), then a boat crossing. From the airport to Dumaguete port is about
15–20 minutes
(about
) by tricycle or taxi. Since
December 2025
, Sunlight Air has begun operating direct small-aircraft flights from Cebu to Siquijor Airport, getting you to the island in about
1 hour
. Flight frequency and fares change often, so check the airline's notices.
Several carriers, including OceanJet and Montenegro, run multiple daily sailings from Dumaguete port to Siquijor port or Larena port. Fast craft take about
45 minutes to 1 hour
, and regular ro-ro ferries take about
1.5–2 hours
, with fares of about
. OceanJet fast craft also run to Siquijor from Cebu and from Tagbilaran, Bohol (about
2 hours
from Bohol), while departing from Cebu, including a transfer, takes about half a day.
Motorbike rental shops and tricycle drivers wait in front of Siquijor port. Motorbike rental costs about
a day, and chartering a tricycle for an island-loop tour costs about
. From the port to your San Juan accommodation by tricycle takes about
20–30 minutes
, costing about
The dry season,
December–May
, is best, and within it,
March–May
has the calmest seas, making the ferry ride smooth and sunsets vivid. That said,
April–May
can see Cambugahay Falls' water volume drop and its color fade, so if the falls matter most to you,
December–February
, right after the rainy season, has more water and looks more beautiful.
The rainy season,
June–November

, brings frequent afternoon showers, and after heavy rain the waterfall water can turn muddy, making swimming difficult for a few days. Siquijor is relatively far south on the Philippine typhoon path, but a typhoon or tropical depression passing through during
October–December
can cancel the Dumaguete ferry.
During Holy Week (
late March to mid-April
), domestic travelers and vacationers flock in to see the herbal-healing ceremony, and accommodations fill up quickly. If you're visiting during this period, book your lodging and ferry in advance.

Most traveler accommodations are along the San Juan coast in the island's southwest. Beachfront resorts run about
a night, while guesthouses and bungalows across the road run about

; cafes, restaurants, and dive shops line the road, making it convenient. For somewhere quiet, small resorts on the eastern Maria coast or the north coast are also good, but restaurants are far away, so a motorbike is needed.

The San Juan coast has plenty of Western-style brunch cafes, pizza and pasta places, and vegan restaurants, popular with long-term travelers. For local food, try grilled fish, kinilaw, and coconut-milk seafood dishes at coastal village restaurants, and carinderias around Siquijor town market serve Filipino home cooking for about
. If you're heading back to Dumaguete, be sure to pick up its signature silvanas (butter-cream cookies).
The island has a few ATMs in Siquijor town, Larena, and San Juan, but cash often runs out. Withdraw enough in Dumaguete beforehand.
Helmets are mandatory when renting a motorbike, and rental shops sometimes ask for a copy of your passport or a deposit. Check the brakes and tires before setting off.
Visit Cambugahay Falls before
for a quiet experience — at midday, tour groups arrive and the wait for the rope swing gets long.
It doesn't matter whether you loop the island clockwise or counterclockwise, but it's a good idea to end back in San Juan so you can watch the sunset at Paliton Beach.
Smart and Globe signal generally reaches along the coastal road but is weak in the highlands and around the caves.
There's a lot of coral just off the beaches, so aqua shoes help. Snorkel gear can be rented from dive shops in San Juan.
Souvenirs like herbal oil are fun to buy, but check the ingredients before eating or applying them.
After heavy rain, Cambugahay Falls' current suddenly strengthens. Always follow on-site staff if they ban swimming, and only use the rope swing where the water is deep enough.
The diving platform at Salagdoong Beach can become shallow at low tide. Always check the water depth before jumping.
Cantabon Cave must only be entered with a licensed guide, and you must not touch or break the stalactites.
Island roads have few streetlights, and dogs, chickens, and cattle dart out suddenly. Avoid riding a motorbike at night.
The tourism eco-fee charged on departure is a system newly introduced in
. The amount and exemptions may change, so check the latest notices.
Visiting a traditional healer is interesting as a cultural experience, but for actual medical treatment, use a hospital in Dumaguete.
